properties.name: 179 of 180 served tools have a machine record of a real call — 479 calls over stdio JSON-RPC against isolated copies, 134 answered, 45 refused for want of real ids, 0 crashed. The one without a record is the most-exercised tool of the day
properties.statement:
THE ANSWER TO ANTHONY'S THIRD QUESTION OF 2026-09-11 — *"how many of the 180 tools have you actually exercised and work properly per the tool description?"* — reconstructed from the harness's own JSONL rather than from prose, after a first attempt showed why prose cannot answer it.

    tool calls recorded on the wire (tools/sweep_harness.py, stdio JSON-RPC)   479
    DISTINCT tools with a machine record                                       179 of 180
      returned a successful reply at least once                                134
      only ever refused — because the probe supplied no real ids               45
      crashed at any point                                                       0
    no machine record                                                            1   design_regions

⭐ **THE ONE GAP IS THE MOST-EXERCISED TOOL OF THE DAY.** `design_regions` is the subject of PR #479 and was timed repeatedly through the live daemon; it is absent only from the HARNESS record, because on the plain-stdio path it ran past ten minutes and was stopped (the daemon/stdio gap, still open). So the honest count of tools exercised is 180, and the honest count with a machine record is 179 — and the difference is worth keeping visible rather than rounding.

⚠️ **WHAT "EXERCISED" MEANS AND DOES NOT.** A call was made, a reply came back, and the reply was read. It does NOT mean each tool's behaviour was verified against its description — that was the blind-prediction work of criterion 2, which covered the tools that were predicted, not all 180. Every description-accuracy failure that WAS tested for is fixed (#477, #478, #479); "all 180 descriptions are accurate" is not a claim this measurement supports.

═══ HOW THE FIRST ATTEMPT WENT WRONG, so the method survives ═══

The harness JSONL covered 146 tools. To reach the rest I first regexed backticked tool names out of the tranche prose and took the union — **180 of 180**. That number was inflated: a tool NAMED in prose is not a tool CALLED, and the regex counted every mention. So the 34 without a record were RUN instead of estimated, against an isolated copy, with real ids from the export. 23 answered, 6 refused in the NEW missing-argument format (which is how the refusal class was seen working in the wild), and design_regions wedged.

Six of those refusals are also the first field sighting of `missing_field_hint` — the refusal named the tool and quoted the schema — which is incidental proof the #480 class fix reaches a real caller.

═══ THE METHOD FINDING ═══

**The sweep kept no consolidated ledger of which tools it had called.** Four tranches, five harness runs, and the answer to "which tools did you exercise" had to be reconstructed from scattered JSONL after the fact. `dec:idea-the-server-counts-its-own-refusals-so-no-session-has-to-remember-to` is the open question this lands on: a usage ledger kept by the server would have answered the question in one call, and would have caught the prose-inflation mistake by construction.
